title: Wheel stuck
cause: A drive wheel is blocked by hair, a cable or the robot is stuck on an obstacle.
solution: Lift the robot, remove hair and debris from both drive wheels, check that the wheels turn freely, place the robot on a flat floor and press Power / Clean.

title: Main brush tangled
cause: Hair, string or a cable is wrapped around the main brush.
solution: Remove the main brush cover, take out the main brush, cut tangled hair with the cleaning tool blade, clean the brush ends and reinstall.

title: Side brush stuck
cause: The side brush cannot rotate (usually tangled hair or threads).
solution: Unscrew the side brush, remove hair from the shaft and brush, reinstall it. Replace the side brush if its bristles are bent.

title: Cliff sensor dirty or blocked
cause: The cliff sensors under the robot are dirty or the robot is on a very dark/reflective surface.
solution: Wipe all cliff sensors with a dry soft cloth. If the error appears only on dark carpets, move the robot to another area or add a no-go zone.

title: Bumper stuck
cause: The front bumper is pressed or jammed by debris.
solution: Tap the bumper several times gently, remove any debris between the bumper and the body, and make sure it moves freely.

title: LiDAR sensor blocked
cause: The LiDAR cover on top of the robot is blocked or cannot rotate, or the robot is stuck under low furniture.
solution: Check that nothing is on top of the LiDAR cover, press the cover gently to make sure it moves, remove dust around it. Move the robot out from under furniture lower than 10 cm. False E06 errors in bright sunlight were fixed in firmware 2.3.0 — update the firmware.

title: Battery too low to return
cause: The battery level is too low for the robot to find its way back to the dock.
solution: Carry the robot to the charging dock manually and let it charge. Make sure the dock is placed according to the installation instructions.

title: Dustbin missing
cause: The dustbin is not installed or not fully inserted.
solution: Insert the dustbin until it clicks into place.

title: Water tank empty or missing
cause: The mopping module is attached but the water tank is empty or not detected.
solution: Refill the water tank with clean cold water, make sure the module clicks into place. If mopping is not needed, remove the module.

title: Charging error
cause: Charging contacts are dirty, the dock has no power, or the battery temperature is outside 0–40 °C.
solution: Clean the charging contacts on the robot and the dock with a dry cloth, check the dock power cable, move the robot to a room with normal temperature. If the error persists, contact Orbitra support.

title: Water tank empty
cause: The water tank is empty or not inserted correctly.
solution: Fill the water tank with fresh cold water and push it in completely until it clicks.

title: Bean hopper empty
cause: There are no beans in the hopper or the beans are stuck.
solution: Refill the bean hopper. If beans are present, stir them gently — oily beans can stick together.

title: Brew group missing
cause: The brew group is not inserted or the service door is open.
solution: Insert the brew group correctly (the lever must be in the lowest position) and close the service door.

title: Grinder blocked
cause: The grinder is blocked by a foreign object, flavoured/oily beans or ground coffee was put into the hopper.
solution: Switch off and unplug the machine, empty the bean hopper and vacuum it. Never put ground or caramelised beans in the hopper. If the error persists, contact Orbitra support — do not try to open the grinder yourself.

title: Drip tray or grounds container full
cause: The drip tray or the grounds container is full or not inserted.
solution: Empty and rinse the drip tray and the grounds container and insert them back. Wait at least 5 seconds before reinserting so the counter is reset.

title: Descaling required
cause: The calculated amount of limescale has reached the limit.
solution: Run the descaling program with Orbitra DecalPro (about 25 minutes). The machine can still be used for a short time but descaling should be done as soon as possible.

title: Temperature sensor or heater fault
cause: The heating system is overheated or the temperature sensor is defective.
solution: Switch off the machine, unplug it and let it cool down for 30 minutes. If C7 appears again, stop using the machine and contact Orbitra support.

title: Milk system blocked
cause: Dried milk residue is blocking the milk tube or frother.
solution: Disassemble and wash the milk frother and tube in warm water, then run the Milk Clean program. Run Milk Clean after every milk drink to prevent this.

title: Fan motor fault
cause: The fan motor does not reach the required speed.
solution: Unplug the purifier for 1 minute and plug it in again. Make sure nothing blocks the air outlet. If F1 persists, contact Orbitra support.

title: PM2.5 sensor fault
cause: The PM2.5 sensor is dirty or defective; Auto mode cannot work.
solution: Clean the sensor lens with a dry cotton swab (sensor cover on the side of the device). If the error persists, contact Orbitra support. Manual speeds still work.

title: Filter not installed
cause: The filter cartridge is not detected or the bottom cover is not closed properly.
solution: Insert the filter cartridge (remove its plastic wrapping) and close the bottom cover until it locks.

title: Filter expired
cause: The filter cartridge has reached 0% of its life.
solution: Replace the filter cartridge with a genuine Orbitra A5 cartridge and reset the filter counter by holding the Timer button for 5 seconds.

title: No power / low voltage
cause: The C-wire is not connected, loose, or the transformer provides less than 20 V AC.
solution: Switch off HVAC power, check the C and R wires at the thermostat and at the HVAC unit. If there is no C-wire, install the Orbitra Power Adapter PA-1.

title: Temperature sensor fault
cause: The internal temperature sensor reports invalid values.
solution: Restart the thermostat by removing the display from the base plate for 10 seconds. If H2 persists, contact Orbitra support.

title: Wi-Fi connection lost
cause: The thermostat cannot connect to the Wi-Fi network.
solution: Check that your router works and broadcasts a 2.4 GHz network. Reconnect via Menu › Settings › Wi-Fi › Change network. The thermostat keeps following the last saved schedule offline.

title: HVAC system not responding
cause: The room temperature has not changed within 30 minutes after heating or cooling was requested.
solution: Check that the HVAC system is switched on and its breaker is not tripped, check the HVAC filter and the wiring of W (heat) and Y (cool) terminals. Contact your HVAC technician if the system itself is faulty.

title: Wiring error
cause: Wires are connected to the wrong terminals (for example both W and Y missing, or O/B configured incorrectly for a heat pump).
solution: Switch off HVAC power and check the wiring against the photo of your old thermostat. Rerun the setup wizard and select the correct system type.
